unit.title: JavaScript: numbers and text
unit.description: Calculating with + - * / and %, joining text, mixing text and numbers, length, capital letters

cards.definition: The symbols that calculate: + adds, - subtracts, * multiplies, / divides.
Joining pieces of text end to end with the + sign.
Gives what is left after a whole division: 7 % 3 gives 1.
cards.example: n % 2 === 0 tells you that n is even.

cards.definition: Gives how many characters a piece of text has, spaces included, or how many items a list holds.
Returns a copy of a text written in capital letters; the original text does not change.
Converts a text such as "42" into a value you can calculate with, so that + adds instead of joining.

exercises.explain: * is the multiplication sign in JavaScript (not x), and / divides.
whyWrong: * multiplies; it does not glue the digits together.
10 would be 7 + 3; * multiplies.
4 would be 7 - 3; * multiplies.

exercises.explain: With text, + joins the pieces end to end: this is concatenation. Spaces inside the quotes are kept.
whyWrong: The space is inside the first text, so it is kept.
The + sign is applied, it is not printed.
Joining two texts with + is allowed.

exercises.explain: As soon as one side of + is text, JavaScript joins instead of adding: "5" + 2 gives "52". A classic trap with form fields.
whyWrong: "5" is text, so + joins instead of adding.
Nothing is added: the result is the text 52.
JavaScript does not stop: it turns 2 into text.

exercises.explain: Text and variables can be joined with +. name is replaced by its value, "Ana".
whyWrong: name without quotes is the variable: its value is used.
The + signs join the pieces; they are not printed.
The "!" is joined at the end as well.

exercises.explain: .length gives the number of characters of a text. Spaces count too.
whyWrong: Count the letters: S, a, l, e.
It is one text, but .length counts its characters.
.length gives a number, not the text.

exercises.explain: % gives the remainder: 3 fits 3 times in 10 (that makes 9), and 1 is left. Handy to test even numbers: n % 2 === 0.
whyWrong: % is not a division: it gives what is left over.
3 is how many times 3 fits in 10; % gives what is left.
10 is not a multiple of 3, so something is left over.

exercises.explain: Number() turns the text "8" into the number 8, so + adds instead of joining.

exercises.prompt: Build a line that prints the result of 12 divided by 4.
exercises.explain: In JavaScript, / divides and * multiplies. console.log(12 / 4) prints 3.
toUpperCase() gives a copy written in capital letters. toLowerCase() does the opposite.
whyWrong: toUpperCase() returns the text in capital letters.
Every letter becomes a capital, not just the first one.
The value of word is used, not its name.

exercises.prompt: The total should be 30, but the console shows 1020. Which line causes it?
exercises.explain: price holds the text "10" because of the quotes, so + joins: "10" + 20 gives "1020". Write let price = 10; without quotes.

exercises.prompt: Build a line that prints "Hi " joined with the variable name.
exercises.explain: console.log("Hi " + name) joins the text and the value of name.
